title: Mushroom and Swiss Smash Burger
changes_from_base: Same smash method as the Classic. Garlic-thyme mushrooms are browned first in the same pan, Swiss replaces American cheese, and the sauce is a lemony garlic mayo with peppery rocket instead of lettuce and pickles.
summary: Earthy pan-fried mushrooms and melted Swiss cheese turn the classic smash burger into something richer, finished with a light garlic mayo and peppery rocket.
equipment: large cast-iron or heavy steel frying pan (at least 26 cm) or flat griddle
stiff metal spatula (fish slice or burger turner)

ingredients.item: chestnut or white mushrooms, thinly sliced
soft burger buns or brioche-style buns

steps.title: Make the garlic mayo
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise with the grated garlic and a squeeze of lemon, then set it aside. Resting it for a few minutes lets the raw garlic mellow slightly so it doesn't overpower the mushrooms and beef later.

steps.title: Cook the mushrooms
steps.text: Melt the butter in the large frying pan over medium-high heat, spread the mushrooms out in a single layer, and leave them untouched for 3-4 minutes so they release their water. Stir and cook for a further 3-4 minutes until deeply golden, working in two batches if your pan is smaller than 28cm so the mushrooms don't steam instead of browning.

steps.title: Season and finish the mushrooms
steps.text: Add salt only once the mushrooms are browned, since salting them early draws out moisture and stops them catching colour properly. Stir in the garlic and thyme for a final minute, then tip everything into a bowl and wipe the pan clean.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast them cut-side down in the wiped pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until golden, then set aside. The toasting seals the crumb so the mayo won't soak straight through.

steps.title: Heat the pan and smash
steps.text: Crank the same pan up to high for 4-5 minutes until a flicked drop of water skitters and disappears. Add 2-3 beef balls, well spaced, cover each with baking paper, and press hard with a spatula for 20-30 seconds until flattened to about 6mm - then don't press again.

steps.title: Season and sear
steps.text: Peel back the paper and season the tops with salt and pepper. Sear undisturbed for 2-2.5 minutes until the underside builds a deep, lacy brown crust, which is where most of the savoury flavour in a smash burger comes from.

steps.title: Flip and top with mushrooms and Swiss
steps.text: Scrape firmly underneath to lift the crust, flip, and spoon the cooked mushrooms over half the patties before laying Swiss cheese on top. Cook for 45-60 seconds, covering the pan for 30 seconds if the cheese needs encouragement to melt; the melting Swiss holds the mushrooms in place and the beef should reach 71°C with clear juices.

steps.title: Build the burger
steps.text: Spread the garlic mayo on both toasted bun halves and add a handful of rocket to the bottom one. Stack the mushroom-and-Swiss patty with a plain patty on top, then finish with the top bun.

tips: Don't crowd the mushrooms - if your pan is smaller than about 28cm, cook them in two batches so they brown instead of stewing in their own liquid.
Salt the mushrooms only after they've browned; salting raw mushrooms draws out water and stops them catching colour.
Don't press the patties more than once - a second press squeezes out the juices that keep the burger moist.
Wipe the pan before smashing the beef so leftover mushroom butter doesn't scorch at high heat.
storage: Cooked patties and mushrooms keep together in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days; the beef also freezes well for up to 2 months. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot throughout and the centre reaches 74°C, and dress with fresh mayo and rocket rather than storing them assembled.
